title: Record that one unsplit call per stage still needs thin rank 8
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Over F_2, at block size 2 and three paired leaves, one unsplit full call on each stage does not let two constant thin maps meet the paired-star endpoint at total rank 6 or 7. Every solution has rank sum at least 8, and 8 is attained by an explicit word in each of the two affine families. Ranks 6 and 7 miss the endpoint.

This is a scoped identity in `F_2[D_0, D_1, D_2, e] / (e^2)`. It is not a caller and not a kappa improvement. The selected frontier stays `781451/250000000 = 0.003125804` from PR #6030. No κ change is claimed.

The pure factors are `I + x_j E_j`. They already match the pure target, which is the count left open by the three-or-more projector obstruction. The e coefficient is an entrywise two-gap equation. Eighteen of the 36 order-and-gap systems are impossible because a defect monomial is outside the span of the two gap monomials. The other eighteen are leaf permutations of two families. Family A has a block-rank proof. Family B is the full affine space of eight 2-by-2 matrices, and the compiled census visits all `2^32` points. A branch is skipped only when six leaf rows, independent of the two core parameters, already have rank sum at least 8.

## Task and overlap

Base commit: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (canonical CrocSwap `main`). This draft uses `cursor/upstream-17469fff-pin-0214` as its base because that branch is the same commit; the fork's own `main` is older. The upstream target is CrocSwap `main`.

Task card: `joint-query-controller`, scope refined. The card asks whether a changed caller or query demand removes real work. This package answers the one-unsplit-call question left by merged PR #6956. It is not a caller and it does not change kappa.

Nearest overlap, rechecked against open upstream PRs and Discussions #1166 and #5593:

- PR #5747 is the contract, the rank floor of 6, and the commuting rank-8 construction.
- Merged PR #6922 shows that one F_2 thin map misses the endpoint on the two-call contract.
- Merged PR #6940 shows that every two-map F_2 word on the two-call contract has total rank at least 8.
- Merged PR #6956 shows that three or more T-commuting full calls miss the pure endpoint, and leaves this one-unsplit-call equation open. This package starts from the three factors `I + x_j E_j` and does not redo that projector obstruction.
- Open PR #7011 exhibits three F_2 thin maps of ranks 2+2+2 on the two-call contract. It does not place one unsplit call on each stage.
- Open PRs #7006, #7010, and #7005 are the partial F_4 census, the adjacent-halves count, and the consecutive-word rank floor. None of them is this gap equation.

## Validation

Python 3.12 and gcc. From the repository root:

```
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-star-unsplit-two-thin
```

Registered status: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with outcome `negative-result`. The replay runs `verify.py` and then the same check under `python3 -O -B`. Both printed `PASS_PAIRED_STAR_UNSPLIT_TWO_THIN` with `impossible=18`, `family_A=12`, `family_B=6`, `one_thin_hits=0`, `min_rank_sum_A=8`, `min_rank_sum_B=8`, `family_B_count=4294967296`, and witness ranks `4+4`. Failures are raised, so `-O` does not strip them.

The polynomial word was compared with the conjugation formula on every order and every gap pair. The zero-parameter words of both families equal the target. A shared diagonal block still matches; the same block on only one map, and either map deleted, misses the target. No Lean proof, Docker replay, `make frontier6030-verify`, or selected-frontier replay was run.

## Credit

The contract, the rank floor, and the commuting construction are from PR #5747 (Ali Romman), including the predecessor statements in PR #5673, PR #5631, and PR #5617. The one-unsplit-call opening is PR #6956. The two-call rank-8 census is PR #6940. The one-map obstruction is PR #6922. Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Independent human review and a proof-assistant proof are unclaimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

- With the same one unsplit call on each stage, can three constant F_2 thin maps meet total rank 6? Two maps now need 8, so the chronological floor of 6 is still open under this call shape. Fix order `(0, 1, 2)`, place the maps in three distinct gaps, and solve the three-term entry equation. PR #7011 does not answer this: its word uses two full calls per stage.
- Can a thin map with entries in `F_2[D_0, D_1, D_2]` bring the unsplit two-map rank below 8? The constant census does not apply. Let one diagonal block be linear in a single `D_j` and test the same two gap families.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The pure factors are diagonal, so the two-gap equation separates by matrix entry and the affine space is exact. The useful check was that separation, followed by one block-rank proof and one finite census. Feedback discussion: #1200
